review_method: Re-review all eight categories and nine vetoes using dated harness raw/evidence, reconcile latest/checkpoint differences, recompute cash scenarios and reverse expectations, refresh dated prices, retain unaffected judgments and document every score change. No macro-score mixing.
portfolio_context: No actual holding, tax lot, liquidity need or portfolio risk budget supplied. This research does not authorize a trade.
structural_thesis: Samsung Biologics remains a scale-leading biologics CDMO with a credible long-duration demand runway, expanding from antibodies into ADC, mRNA and peptides while adding U.S./European manufacturing exposure.
customer_and_moat: Large validated capacity, regulatory track record, technology-transfer friction and customer switching costs remain meaningful advantages. Moat durability depends on quality, utilization, batch economics and the ability to integrate new modalities without diluting returns on capital.
current_finding: H1 2026 continuing revenue was KRW 2.578tn and operating income KRW 1.167tn. Q2 revenue was KRW 1.321tn and operating profit KRW 0.586tn; management expects the upper end of +15-20% 2026 revenue growth guidance. The Aug-28 KRW 3tn rights offering introduces 2.27m new shares and must be included in per-share valuation.
economic_finding: The core CDMO business is highly profitable, but PolyPeptide is still in a heavy reinvestment phase: H1 2026 revenue +41.6% and EBITDA margin 20.7%, yet disclosed FCF was -EUR 19.1m and net debt EUR 90.2m. The acquisition therefore adds strategic option value but not immediately proven high-return owner cash flow.
capital_and_survival: Equity financing preserves balance-sheet resilience better than debt funding, but it is real external capital. Pro-forma shares rise from 46.291m to 48.561m, about 4.9%. Existing holders can preserve ownership through rights participation, but management must earn an adequate return on roughly KRW 3tn of new equity capital.
next_evidence: Final rights-offering terms and subscription results; PolyPeptide tender acceptance and closing; purchase-price allocation and funding bridge; Plant 5/Rockville utilization and margin progression; consolidated post-deal FCF, working capital and incremental ROIC; customer concentration disclosure.
permanent_loss_case: A permanent-loss path exists if the market capitalizes a decade of high growth while Plant 5/Rockville utilization, pricing or quality execution weakens and the PolyPeptide integration absorbs additional capital without durable FCF. In that case strong accounting profit could coexist with materially lower per-share economic value.
falsifiers: Plant 5/Rockville utilization, yield or collection economics fail to improve over four reporting periods while capacity continues to expand.
Material quality/regulatory failure causes customer loss or persistent pricing concessions.
PolyPeptide integration requires materially more capital than announced and does not show a credible path to positive FCF and acceptable incremental ROIC.
Customer or modality concentration becomes severe enough that one program/regulation can impair the long-term earnings base.
Current valuation rises to require the internal bull case or better under conservative cash assumptions.
increase_evidence: Two or more reporting periods showing Plant 5/Rockville ramp with stable or improving cash conversion.
PolyPeptide closes without material financing slippage and demonstrates improving FCF/ROIC after integration.
Post-rights pro-forma valuation offers a meaningful expectation gap under conservative base assumptions rather than requiring the bull case.
All INVESTIGATE veto items have specific primary-source evidence sufficient to reduce uncertainty.
sell_evidence: Persistent quality/regulatory failures or clear moat shrinkage.
Repeated external equity funding becomes necessary to sustain growth without commensurate per-share FCF growth.
Incremental ROIC structurally deteriorates after the current expansion cycle.

evidence: Large-scale biologics outsourcing remains structurally attractive; Samsung is expanding capacity, geography and modalities.
counter_evidence: Industry capacity additions and customer bargaining power can reduce returns if demand growth disappoints.

evidence: Validated large-scale manufacturing, regulatory execution and switching friction provide strong customer value.
counter_evidence: CDMO relationships remain commercially negotiated and are not immune to pricing or quality competition.

evidence: Scale, order history, global footprint and broader modality coverage can widen the moat.
counter_evidence: The moat widens only if new capacity and acquisitions sustain quality, utilization and returns.

evidence: Core continuing operations show high operating profitability and strong H1 operating cash flow.
counter_evidence: Plant 5/Rockville are still ramping; PolyPeptide H1 FCF was negative and the new KRW 3tn equity capital has not yet demonstrated its incremental return.

evidence: Equity funding limits leverage risk and the PolyPeptide asset has strong peptide-growth exposure.
counter_evidence: The acquisition carries a 40% premium to the unaffected price and requires a large rights offering; integration and return-on-new-equity are unproven.

evidence: H1 balance sheet was resilient and equity funding avoids a large debt-funded acquisition burden.
counter_evidence: Growth is capital intensive and the rights offering confirms that internal cash alone is not being used to finance the present expansion package.

evidence: At KRW 1.405m, the updated bridge values are roughly KRW 0.377m bear, KRW 1.159m base and KRW 2.398m bull per share.

hard_vetoes.evidence: No material integrity/accounting trigger identified in reviewed filings and current official disclosures.
KRW 3tn rights offering funds PolyPeptide and Bio Campus II. One strategic rights issue is not yet structural excessive dependence, but it is material external financing.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Assess whether future capacity/M&A can be funded by internally generated cash after the current cycle.

hard_vetoes.evidence: Current offering is approximately 4.9% of pre-offering shares and is structured as a rights offering. No evidence yet of long-duration excessive dilution.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Monitor recurrence and per-share FCF growth.

hard_vetoes.evidence: Core growth is backed by contracted manufacturing activity and capacity utilization rather than pure subsidy/marketing spend.
Large new capacity and acquisition capital are not yet mature enough for a reliable cohort incremental-ROIC test; PolyPeptide H1 FCF was negative.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Measure post-ramp and post-acquisition NOPAT/owner cash against incremental invested capital.

hard_vetoes.evidence: No current evidence of persistent competitive-advantage contraction; capacity/geography/modality breadth is expanding.
Reference price is above the internal base bridge but below the internal bull bridge; price does not mechanically require bull-or-better, though the expectation gap is weak.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Refresh with a full pro-forma DCF after rights and PolyPeptide closing.

hard_vetoes.evidence: Samsung customer concentration is incompletely disclosed in current evidence; PolyPeptide H1 revenue was 68.4% metabolic therapeutics, increasing modality concentration risk.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Obtain customer/program concentration and contract economics after consolidation.

hard_vetoes.evidence: Business survivability is strong, but valuation duration plus heavy capital deployment can create permanent per-share loss without bankruptcy.
hard_vetoes.resolution_needed: Re-underwrite after final financing, acquisition close and evidence of new-capital returns.

valuation_summary.method: Bridge from the 2026-09-06 operating scenarios to the announced rights issue; not a standalone valuation of PolyPeptide.

final_rationale: WATCH. Samsung Biologics remains a high-quality structural compounder candidate, but the investment case is currently constrained by a weak expectation gap and a newly material capital-allocation test. The KRW 3tn rights offering does not by itself trigger a hard reject because it is a rights issue used for strategic assets and preserves balance-sheet resilience; however, it raises the burden of proof on incremental ROIC and per-share FCF. Score falls from 70 to 68, driven by lower incremental-ROIC and management/capital-allocation scores. No new-buy authorization until the financing and acquisition close and the new capital demonstrates acceptable economic returns.
